goal: Forward deployed engineer ready by April 2027

phases.title: System design foundations
phases.why: FDEs design systems on the spot with a customer in the room. You need the building blocks cold so you can spend your energy on the customer's problem.
phases.gate: Whiteboard 6 classic designs end to end in 45 minutes each, and publish a write-up of the best one.

weeks.title: The interview framework and the numbers

tasks.task: Read Hello Interview's 'How to Prepare' and 'Delivery Framework'. Write the 5-step framework (requirements, entities, API, high-level design, deep dives) on an index card.
Learn the numbers: memory vs SSD vs network latency, QPS one Postgres box handles, Redis ops/sec. Make a one-page cheat sheet in your own words.
Do 3 back-of-envelope estimates: daily storage for WhatsApp messages, peak QPS for a ticket sale, bandwidth for 1M concurrent video viewers. Show your math.
Networking essentials: TCP vs UDP, HTTP/2, WebSockets vs SSE vs long polling, L4 vs L7 load balancers. Write when you'd pick each.
Read DDIA chapter 1 (reliability, scalability, maintainability). Note the Twitter fan-out example: you'll reuse it all phase.

weeks.challenge: Watch Hello Interview's Bitly breakdown, then close it and design Bitly yourself in 45 minutes. Compare.

weeks.title: APIs, data modeling and indexing

tasks.task: API design: REST resource naming, pagination (offset vs cursor), idempotent POST. Design the API for a food-delivery app's orders.
Data modeling: relational vs document vs wide-column. Model the same orders domain twice (Postgres and DynamoDB) and list the tradeoffs.
Indexing: B-tree vs LSM tree vs hash vs geospatial index. Run EXPLAIN on a Postgres query before and after adding an index.
Read DDIA chapter 3 (storage and retrieval) and write 5 bullets on why LSM trees win on writes.
Postgres deep dive: MVCC, when one box is enough, read replicas. Most customer systems you'll meet run on Postgres.

weeks.challenge: Design the schema, indexes and API for a Ticketmaster-style event booking system, then check it against the Hello Interview breakdown.

weeks.title: Caching, Redis and scaling reads

tasks.task: Caching strategies: cache-aside, write-through, write-behind, TTLs, invalidation, stampede protection. Draw where each sits.
Redis deep dive: data structures, sorted sets for leaderboards, Redis as a lock and as a rate limiter.
Scaling reads pattern: replicas, caches, CDNs, denormalization. Apply it to a product catalog with 100x more reads than writes.
Code an LRU cache with TTL in Python or TypeScript with tests (LeetCode 146 plus expiry).
Real-world read: how Discord moved trillions of messages and used request coalescing for hot partitions.

resources.title: Discord: How we store trillions of messages

weeks.challenge: Design the Facebook News Feed (fan-out on write vs read, caching the feed). Compare with Hello Interview's breakdown.

weeks.title: Replication, sharding and consistent hashing

tasks.task: Watch Kleppmann's distributed systems lectures 1 to 3 (why distributed systems, the two generals, time and clocks).
Read DDIA chapter 5 (replication). Explain replication lag and read-your-writes to an imaginary customer whose edits 'disappear'.
Sharding: choosing a shard key, hot partitions, cross-shard queries. Pick shard keys for chat, orders and analytics events.
Consistent hashing with virtual nodes. Implement it in under 80 lines and measure key movement when adding a node.
Cassandra deep dive: leaderless replication, quorums (R + W > N), tunable consistency.

weeks.challenge: Design WhatsApp (1:1 and group chat, delivery receipts, offline users). Compare with Hello Interview's breakdown.

weeks.title: Consistency, transactions and contention

tasks.task: CAP and PACELC in practice: which parts of a booking system need strong consistency and which can be eventual?
Dealing with contention: pessimistic locks, optimistic concurrency, distributed locks. Solve the 'last seat' double-booking problem three ways.
Read Kleppmann on distributed locking and fencing tokens. Write down why a Redis lock alone is not safe.

resources.title: Kleppmann: How to do distributed locking

tasks.task: Sagas vs 2PC for multi-service workflows. Sketch a saga for 'charge card, reserve stock, book courier' with compensations.
Raft: play the visualization end to end, then explain leader election and log replication in 5 sentences.

resources.title: The Secret Lives of Data: Raft

weeks.challenge: Design a payment system that never double-charges. Compare with Hello Interview's Payment System breakdown.

weeks.title: Queues, streams and async work

tasks.task: Read Jay Kreps's 'The Log': why an append-only log is the backbone of data integration.
Kafka deep dive: partitions, consumer groups, ordering, retention, exactly-once in practice.
Outbox pattern and change data capture: how to update a DB and publish an event without losing either.
Long-running tasks: job queues, workers, retries, dead letter queues, durable workflows (Temporal). Agents will need all of this later.

resources.title: Hello Interview: Managing Long Running Tasks

tasks.task: Avoiding queue backlogs: read the Amazon Builders' Library article and list 3 tactics.

weeks.challenge: Design a distributed job scheduler. Compare with Hello Interview's Job Scheduler breakdown.

weeks.title: Reliability, rate limiting and design practice

tasks.task: Timeouts, retries with exponential backoff and jitter, circuit breakers. Write a retry helper with jitter.

resources.title: Amazon: Timeouts, retries and backoff with jitter

tasks.task: Rate limiting: token bucket vs sliding window. Implement a sliding-window limiter on Redis.

resources.title: Stripe: Scaling your API with rate limiters

tasks.task: SLIs, SLOs and error budgets. Write an SLO for an API you've built at work.

resources.title: Google SRE book: Service Level Objectives

tasks.task: Read 3 public postmortems and write the root cause and the fix for each in one line.
Design ChatGPT as a system (streaming, conversation storage, GPU capacity). This is the bridge into phase 2.

weeks.challenge: Phase capstone: record yourself designing Dropbox in 45 minutes, then publish your best design of the phase as a write-up with diagrams.

phases.title: LLM application engineering
phases.why: Most FDE roles now ship LLM features into customer workflows. You need to build, measure and cost them like any production system.
phases.gate: Ship a RAG app with an eval suite and a written cost and latency model.

weeks.title: How LLMs work, and your first API calls

tasks.task: Watch Karpathy's 'Deep Dive into LLMs like ChatGPT' (first half): pretraining, tokens, sampling.

resources.title: Karpathy: Deep Dive into LLMs like ChatGPT

tasks.task: Watch the second half: post-training, RLHF, hallucinations, tool use. Write 5 things that will change how you prompt.

resources.title: Karpathy: Deep Dive into LLMs like ChatGPT

tasks.task: Read The Illustrated Transformer and explain attention in 5 sentences, no math.
Get an API key and work through Anthropic API fundamentals: messages, system prompts, parameters, streaming.
Learn model choice, pricing, rate limits and error handling. Make a table of when you'd use Haiku, Sonnet or Opus for a customer.

weeks.challenge: Build a CLI that summarizes any URL with the Claude API, with streaming output and retry on rate limits.

weeks.title: Prompt engineering for real workloads

tasks.task: Do chapters 1 to 4 of Anthropic's interactive prompt engineering tutorial.
Finish chapters 5 to 9: XML tags, examples, letting the model think, chaining prompts.
Work through 'Real world prompting': a customer-support prompt and a medical-record summarizer.
Read Lilian Weng's prompt engineering survey for the research behind the techniques.
Take a messy prompt from work or a side project and rewrite it. Score both versions on 20 inputs in a spreadsheet.

weeks.challenge: Build a support-ticket classifier (category, urgency, summary) and report accuracy on 30 hand-labeled tickets.

weeks.title: Tool use and structured output

tasks.task: Read the tool use overview and implement a single tool end to end (a weather or calculator tool).
Do the Anthropic tool use course: multiple tools, tool results, the tool-use loop.
Structured outputs: extract invoice fields into a JSON schema and validate with Pydantic or Zod.
Read 'Writing effective tools for agents' and redesign your tools using its advice.

resources.title: Anthropic: Writing effective tools for agents

tasks.task: Take the 'Building with the Claude API' course modules on tool use and RAG (free, with certificate).

resources.title: Anthropic Academy: Building with the Claude API

weeks.challenge: Build an assistant with 3 tools over a real API (GitHub, a calendar, or a public weather API).

weeks.title: Embeddings, vector search and RAG

tasks.task: Read Vicki Boykis's 'What are embeddings' (sections 1 to 4).
Vector databases and HNSW: how approximate nearest neighbor search works and what it costs.
Set up pgvector locally and index 1,000 documents. Time a query.
Chunking strategies: fixed, recursive, semantic. Try two on your corpus and compare retrieval on 10 questions.
Read Anthropic's Contextual Retrieval post (hybrid BM25 plus embeddings plus reranking) and plan how you'd add it.

weeks.challenge: Build a semantic search endpoint over your 1,000 documents with hybrid search.

weeks.title: Evals: the core FDE skill

tasks.task: Read Hamel Husain's 'Your AI product needs evals'.

resources.title: Hamel Husain: Your AI product needs evals

tasks.task: Read the LLM Evals FAQ sections on error analysis and LLM-as-judge.
Error analysis on your own app: read 50 traces, write open notes, then cluster them into failure modes.

resources.title: Hamel: A field guide to improving AI products

tasks.task: Build a golden set of 50 cases with code-based checks and one LLM judge. Calibrate the judge against your own labels.

resources.title: Claude docs: Define success and build evals

tasks.task: Read Anthropic's evals guide for agents and note what changes when the system takes actions.

resources.title: Anthropic: Demystifying evals for AI agents

weeks.challenge: Write an eval suite for your RAG search, run it in CI, and fix the top failure mode.

weeks.title: Production RAG: cost, latency and documents

tasks.task: Read Jason Liu's 'Systematically improving your RAG' and apply the retrieval metrics (recall@k) to your app.

resources.title: Jason Liu: Systematically improving your RAG

tasks.task: Prompt caching: cache your system prompt and documents, then measure cost and latency before and after.
Batch processing for offline jobs, and streaming for interactive ones. Measure time to first token.
PDFs and citations: answer questions over a 50-page PDF with cited passages.
Read 'Patterns for building LLM-based systems' and pick 2 patterns your app is missing.

resources.title: Eugene Yan: Patterns for LLM systems
Applied LLMs: What we learned from a year of building

weeks.challenge: Cut your app's cost per query by 50% without dropping eval scores. Document how.

weeks.title: Build and ship: RAG over a real customer-like corpus

tasks.task: Pick a realistic corpus (a public company's help center or API docs) and write a 1-page 'customer brief': users, questions, success metric.

resources.title: Chip Huyen: AI Engineering book resources

tasks.task: Build ingestion: crawl, chunk, embed, store. Make it re-runnable.
Build the query API and a minimal chat UI with streaming and citations.
Wire your eval suite into CI and add tracing for every request.
Deploy it, write the cost per 1,000 queries and a 'how this scales to 1M queries a day' section.

weeks.challenge: Phase capstone: publish the case study (problem, approach, eval results, cost, tradeoffs) and get one person to use the app.

phases.title: Agents and production AI
phases.why: About a third of FDE postings ask for agent experience and integrating with customer systems. This phase is where you become hireable.
phases.gate: An agent that integrates with a real third-party system, deployed, monitored and evaluated.

weeks.title: Agent patterns from first principles

tasks.task: Read 'Building effective agents' twice. List the 5 workflow patterns and when to use each.
Write an agent loop from scratch (no framework) in under 150 lines: call model, run tools, loop until done.
Read Lilian Weng's 'LLM Powered Autonomous Agents' and Chip Huyen's 'Agents'.

resources.title: Lilian Weng: LLM Powered Autonomous Agents

tasks.task: Do units 1 and 2 of the Hugging Face Agents course to see how frameworks structure the same loop.
Read how Anthropic built its multi-agent research system. Note what broke and how they fixed it.

weeks.challenge: Build an orchestrator-workers agent that researches a company and writes a cited one-page brief, the kind an FDE prepares before a first customer call.

weeks.title: MCP: connecting agents to customer systems

tasks.task: Read the MCP announcement and spec overview: hosts, clients, servers, tools, resources, prompts.
Take Anthropic Academy's 'Introduction to MCP' course.
Do the DeepLearning.AI MCP course: build a server and a client.
Build an MCP server for an API you use at work or daily (Jira, Notion, Linear, Google Sheets) and connect it to Claude Code.
Read 'Code execution with MCP' and 'Advanced tool use' for how to scale to many tools.

weeks.challenge: Publish your MCP server on GitHub with a README and a demo GIF.

weeks.title: Claude Agent SDK and Claude Code as a platform

tasks.task: Read the Agent SDK overview and build the quickstart agent.
Take 'Claude Code in Action' and read the best practices post.

resources.title: Anthropic Academy: Claude Code in Action

tasks.task: Subagents and hooks: add a subagent and a pre-tool-use hook that blocks writes outside one folder.
Agent Skills: package a repeatable workflow (for example 'write a customer weekly update') as a skill.

resources.title: Anthropic: Equipping agents with Agent Skills

tasks.task: Run Claude headless in CI with the GitHub Action.

weeks.challenge: Build a GitHub Action that triages new issues (label, priority, suggested owner) using the Agent SDK.

weeks.title: Context engineering, memory and security

tasks.task: Read 'Effective context engineering for AI agents'. Audit what your agent puts in context and cut 30%.
Long-running agents: read the harness post and add progress notes and a resume-from-checkpoint to your agent.
Prompt injection and the lethal trifecta. Write which of your agents have all three legs.
OWASP Top 10 for LLM apps: map each risk to a control you'd propose to an enterprise security team.
Guardrails and sandboxing: read how Claude Code sandboxes tools and Anthropic's jailbreak mitigation guide.

weeks.challenge: Red-team your own agent: find 3 injection paths and fix them. Write it up as a security note a customer CISO would accept.

weeks.title: Enterprise deployment: cloud, auth, observability

tasks.task: Claude on AWS Bedrock: take the course and call Claude through Bedrock with IAM credentials.

resources.title: Anthropic Academy: Claude with Amazon Bedrock

tasks.task: OAuth 2.0 end to end (authorization code flow, refresh tokens, scopes). Most customer integrations start here.
Webhooks done right: signatures, retries, idempotent handlers.
Tracing for agents: OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions, then instrument your agent with Langfuse.
Containerize your agent with Docker and run it as a queue worker so a 10-minute task survives a restart.

weeks.challenge: Deploy your agent to AWS behind a queue with tracing and a cost, latency and success dashboard.

weeks.title: Build: an agent inside a real workflow

tasks.task: Pick a workflow (support triage in Zendesk, sales research into a CRM, incident summaries into Slack). Write the brief and the success metric first.
Design the evals before the agent: 30 realistic tasks with expected outcomes.

resources.title: Anthropic: Demystifying evals for AI agents

tasks.task: Build the core loop and the integration with OAuth.
Add human approval for risky actions and a kill switch.
Run 100 tasks, report the success rate honestly, record a demo and write the case study.

resources.title: Hamel: A field guide to improving AI products

weeks.challenge: Phase capstone: publish the agent case study and demo it to someone non-technical.

phases.title: The forward deployed role
phases.why: FDEs are hired for judgment with customers as much as for code. This phase turns your projects into customer stories and gets you interviewing.
phases.gate: Two customer-style case studies on this site and 10 applications out.

weeks.title: What FDEs do, and customer discovery

tasks.task: Read the Pragmatic Engineer deep dive on FDEs and Palantir's 'Dev versus Delta'.

resources.title: Pragmatic Engineer: What are Forward Deployed Engineers

tasks.task: Read the analysis of 1,000 FDE job posts. Rate yourself 1 to 5 on the top 10 skills and pick your 2 weakest.
Read The Mom Test summary: how to ask customers questions that don't lie to you.
Interview a friend for 30 minutes about a painful workflow at their job. Map it as steps, tools and handoffs.
Write your 'why FDE' story in 200 words, tied to things you've built.

resources.title: Pragmatic Engineer: What are Forward Deployed Engineers

weeks.challenge: Turn your friend interview into a one-page problem statement with a success metric.

weeks.title: Scoping, design docs and demos

tasks.task: Read Shape Up chapters on shaping and setting appetite. Scope a 4-week pilot for your friend's workflow.
Read 'Design Docs at Google' and write a solution design doc for the pilot.
Add the security and data-handling section an enterprise would ask for (data flow, retention, access, model provider).
Plan a 10-minute demo: problem, before, after, metric, ask. Rehearse it out loud twice.
Record the demo of your phase 3 agent for a pretend customer and watch it back.

resources.title: Pragmatic Engineer: What are Forward Deployed Engineers

weeks.challenge: Publish the pilot proposal and design doc on this site.

weeks.title: Case study 1: an industry workflow end to end

tasks.task: Pick an industry FDEs serve (insurance claims, logistics, legal intake, healthcare ops). Research their workflow and data from public sources.
Write the problem statement, success metric and evals (20 cases).
Build the prototype (extraction plus agent plus integration).
Run evals, fix the top failure, measure impact against the metric.

resources.title: Hamel: A field guide to improving AI products

tasks.task: Write it up as a customer story: situation, approach, result, what you'd do in production.

weeks.challenge: Publish case study 1.

weeks.title: Case study 2: a different customer

tasks.task: Pick a contrasting industry or a contrasting constraint (on-prem data, strict compliance). Research it.

resources.title: Anthropic Academy: Claude with Amazon Bedrock

tasks.task: Write the problem statement, metric and evals.
Build the prototype.
Run evals and measure impact.

resources.title: Anthropic: Demystifying evals for AI agents

tasks.task: Write it up and record a 5-minute demo.

weeks.challenge: Publish case study 2.

weeks.title: Interview prep: decomposition, AI system design, coding

tasks.task: Read the Palantir FDE interview guide and the decomposition guide. Practice 2 decomposition prompts out loud.
AI system design: design an enterprise RAG assistant for 10,000 employees with access control. Out loud, 45 minutes.
AI system design: design an LLM gateway (routing, caching, rate limits, cost tracking, fallbacks).

resources.title: LiteLLM docs (a real gateway to study)

tasks.task: Practical coding: build a small CRUD API plus an LLM call in 60 minutes, timed.
Write 8 STAR stories: ambiguity, conflict, customer pressure, failure, ownership, speed, influence, learning.

weeks.challenge: Do 2 mock interviews with a peer (one decomposition, one AI system design).

weeks.title: Applications and retrospective

tasks.task: Rewrite your resume around customer impact and shipped AI systems.
Update LinkedIn and link this site's case studies.
Send 10 applications to FDE roles at AI labs and AI-first startups.

resources.title: Pragmatic Engineer: What are Forward Deployed Engineers

tasks.task: Reach out to 5 FDEs for a 15-minute chat or referral, with a link to your best case study.
Write the 6-month retrospective: what worked, what you'd skip, what's next.

weeks.challenge: 10 applications sent and your retrospective published on this site.
